title: Getting started
text: Starwake is a ladder: ore -> refined metal -> alloys -> formed and heat-treated parts -> ship components -> a ship. Vanilla smelting still works (vanilla iron counts as plain AISI 1010 steel), so your first machines come from vanilla materials.

Power: burn coal in a Combustion Generator (10 kW) and run Copper Cable to your machines; Solar Panels and Battery Banks come next. Every machine shows its power draw and the grid's supply on its screen.
Pipes move fluids (use an arm touching a tank to make it pull; sneak-use to filter one species). Conveyors and hoppers move items; machines push their outputs into neighbouring inventories.

title: Ore processing
text: Ore is mineral-rich rock: crush it (Jaw Crusher), concentrate it (Flotation Cell with water and pine oil for sulfides, Magnetic Separator for magnetite/ilmenite, Shaking Table for heavy minerals), then roast, smelt and convert.

Copper: chalcopyrite concentrate -> Roasting Kiln (SO2 off-gas) -> Electric Smelter with quartz flux (matte + fayalite slag) -> Converter with oxygen (blister copper). Iron: hematite + coke + limestone in the smelter makes pig iron (C ~4.3%).
Trace elements follow the real chemistry: gold and silver ride with the matte, selenium and tellurium leave as flue dust, lithophile oxides go to the slag. Keep your residues: they are ores too.

title: Wet chemistry
text: The Chemical Reactor, Leach Tank, Evaporator, Crystallizer and Electrolysis Cell work on real mixtures: pipe solutions between them. Catalysts sit in the catalyst slot and are never used up (vanadium for sulfuric acid, iron for ammonia, KOH for electrolysis).

Aluminium: bauxite -> caustic leach -> crystallizer (gibbsite) -> roaster (alumina) -> Hall-Heroult electrolysis with cryolite and carbon (~12.5 kWh per kg). Titanium: ilmenite smelted to titania slag -> Chlorinator with coal + Cl2 (TiCl4) -> Kroll Reactor with magnesium.
Chlor-alkali (brine electrolysis) gives NaOH, Cl2 and H2; the Air Separation Unit gives O2, N2, Ar from whatever air the planet has.

title: Rare elements
text: Every natural element has a real route. Rare earths: crack monazite with NaOH, dissolve in HCl, then the Solvent Extraction Battery (sneak-use to set the cut; re-run products for purity). Platinum metals: anode slimes -> aqua regia -> chloroplatinate. Uranium: acid leach -> yellowcake -> UO2 -> UF4 -> Mg reduction.
Pumps read the biome: oceans give seawater, deserts salt-lake brine (lithium), acid seas acid water. Gas Wells give natural gas with helium. Radioactive material doses you: check the HUD card.

title: Melting and steelmaking
text: The Induction Furnace melts metal items into a bath and taps ingots or 10 kg billets, slabs and castings (moulds). Blow oxygen to burn carbon, silicon and phosphorus in real order (lime flux takes P and S); add argon with the oxygen (AOD) to keep chromium in stainless steel.

Pick a target grade on the screen and the assistant lists exact additions. Reactive metals (Ti, Zr, Nb, Ta...) need the Vacuum Arc Furnace: in air they pick up oxygen and nitrogen. Tungsten and carbides are pressed and sintered (Sintering Press).

title: Forming and heat treatment
text: Rolling Mill: slab -> 10 plates; Wire Drawer: rod -> wire; Extrusion Press: billet -> 20 rods; Forging Press: billet -> forging. Cold passes work-harden (stronger, less ductile) and crack past the alloy's limit: anneal between passes, or switch the mill to HOT.

Heat Treatment Furnace programs: anneal, normalise, harden (water/oil/air quench), temper, solution treat, age, stress relieve. Steel hardens by carbon and hardenability: 4140 hardens through a thick billet in oil where 1045 doesn't. 6061 aluminium needs solution treatment then ageing at ~175 C for T6.

title: Fabrication
text: The Fabricator builds from blueprints (< > on its screen). Each input has gates (minimum strength, service temperature, conductivity...); the panel names the gate an item fails. The main input's alloy is remembered by the product, and its quality is how far the materials beat the gates (up to 1.5, worth up to +20% in a ship part).

Components: pressure vessel, structural frame, combustion chamber (hot alloy + copper liner), nozzle, turbopump (forging), heat exchanger, magnet coil (pure copper wire), control board (microchips, copper wire, solder, gold).

title: Electronics
text: Silicon: quartz + coke in the Submerged Arc Furnace (metallurgical Si) -> Chlorinator with HCl (trichlorosilane distils off, impurities stay) -> Kroll Reactor with H2 (Siemens: electronic-grade Si).

Crystal Puller: electronic-grade silicon (99.999%+) + boron or phosphorus + argon -> 10 doped wafers per kg. Clean Fab: a wafer + the opposite dopant + aluminium or copper wire (99.99%) -> 8 microchips.

title: Ship parts and hulls
text: Every part comes in Mk I, II and III. Mk I parts can still be crafted; all tiers can be fabricated. Mk II/III need components made of better alloys: nozzles rated to 950 C (Inconel 625) for Mk II and 1300 C (C-103 niobium, TZM, tantalum, tungsten) for Mk III.

Hull plating carries its alloy: aluminium is light, steel tougher, superalloys and refractories survive re-entry. Coming in fast heats the leading face; plates rated below the skin temperature burn off (watch SKIN on the HUD). In a crash the face that hits shares the energy; weak blocks break off.

title: Propellants and fusion fuel
text: Fuel tanks take gases from pipes or Gas Cylinders (sneak-use) and burn pairs: hydrogen + oxygen at 1:6, or methane + oxygen at 1:3.6. Hydrogen comes from electrolysis, oxygen from the Air Separation Unit, methane from coke ovens and gas wells.

Quantum and jump drives burn fusion fuel: deuterium + helium-3. Heavy water from the Isotope Column (10 kg of water per cycle), split by electrolysis with KOH; helium-3 from the primordial helium of noble-gas-rich worlds (Air Separation Unit). A few milligrams carry you between planets.

title: Nuclear power
text: Enrich: fluorinate UF4 with F2 in the Roasting Kiln (UF6), spin it in Gas Centrifuges (each pass raises the U-235 share ~1.6x on the abundance ratio; feed the product back in), reduce it with H2, then magnesium.

Fission Reactor: uranium fuel + a moderator. Light water needs ~3% U-235; heavy water runs on natural uranium. Redstone scrams it. Burning breeds plutonium and fills the fuel with fission products: pyroprocess spent fuel in the Electrolysis Cell. The irradiation slot transmutes targets (uranium -> plutonium -> americium -> curium -> berkelium -> californium...; bismuth -> polonium).
Fusion Reactor: 2 MW from deuterium + helium-3. Particle Accelerator: the superheavy elements from real target + beam pairs (oganesson = californium + calcium).

title: Tools, armour and the suit
text: Fabricated tools and armour take every stat from their alloy: hardness sets the mining tier and speed, toughness the durability, strength the damage and protection; dense alloys slow you down. A tempered 4140 pickaxe mines like diamond; mild steel like stone.
Survey Suit upgrades (Fabricator, two of each): lead lining (halves gamma), extra oxygen tank, thermal layer (-100 / +240 C), armour insert.
